A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PFGNet study. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and supplementary Sections 6–9, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PFGNet forecasting results on four main benchmarks and supplementary Moving Fashion-MNIST results, together with ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports PFGNet's own forecasting results on the same five datasets, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and analyses of learned representations.

M1.justification: The encoder–translator–decoder, MSInit, frequency cues, softmax fusion, separable peripheral kernels, learnable center modulation, GLU and rollout procedure remain unchanged. Added channel-allocation detail and clarified notation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Moving MNIST, TaxiBJ, KTH, Human3.6M and supplementary Moving Fashion-MNIST. The KTH prediction horizons and other represented tasks and scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark tables, including supplementary Table 8. Reference renumbering and the new retrospective-cycle-GAN citation do not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 1 retains the same resolutions, temporal windows, model depths, training budgets, learning rates and batch sizes. Dataset splits, metric calculations in Section 7 and supplementary ablation settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both contain the same component, frequency-cue, kernel and depth ablations, learned-beta distributions, TaxiBJ error maps and Human3.6M mechanism visualizations. Repositioning these displays and revising their interpretation add no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The unchanged beta distributions and channel-wise standard deviation describe learned parameters rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Reported benchmark and ablation values, rankings and qualitative examples are unchanged. Examples include Moving MNIST MSE 15.2 and SSIM 0.967 (Table 2), TaxiBJ MSE 0.2881 (Table 3), and Moving Fashion-MNIST MSE 23.55 and SSIM 0.9024 (Table 8).

T1.justification: Section 6 substantially revises both theorems and Lemma 1. Theorem 1 replaces global 'if and only if' positivity with a positive interval bounded by zeros and supplies a new proof. Theorem 2 adds a positive signal-energy assumption, replaces the cubic/unique-maximizer argument with an asymptotic existence proof, and derives a quadratic stationary equation. Lemma 1 adds a nonstationarity condition and replaces its invalid unconditional SNR-improvement argument with a local perturbation proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about biological grounding, frequency-guided adaptivity and efficient forecasting. Their claimed benchmark performance and application scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3.1 qualifies the previously unconditional SNR advantage with 'under mild conditions.' Section 6 softens the interpretation of Figure 10 from validating necessary, maximal denoising to supporting practical denoising flexibility, and no longer asserts that the SNR-improving filter must be ring-shaped.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly specifies that MSInit's projected channels are evenly divided across branches. This adds implementation information without demonstrating a changed implementation. Hardware, training settings, preprocessing descriptions and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kwon and Park's retrospective-cycle-GAN paper, removes TFNet and the bibliographic entry for Seth's TED talk, and adjusts supporting citations for autonomous driving and MetaFormer variants. The broader positioning against prior architectures remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized methodological clarifications, rewrites the supplementary proof exposition, standardizes terminology and bibliography formatting, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section order and main narrative are retained.

P2.justification: All ten tables and fourteen figures are retained, with reflowed placement and spacing. Figure 7 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7, several figure labels change from PFG to PFGNet, and Figure 2 corrects 'DW×3' to 'DW3×3.' No new result display is added.

improvement.justification: The revised proofs remove several invalid inferences and make the SNR advantage appropriately conditional, while the softened interpretation of Figure 10 improves scientific restraint. Remaining inconsistencies limit the gain: Theorem 2 still advertises an SNR maximizer while proving only stationarity, and its final 'at most two' statement overlooks the constant-SNR case it permits. The empirical evidence is retained unchanged.
